passage:
Every morning, a little bird came to the classroom window. It stood on the outside ledge and tapped the glass with its beak.
Some students thought it was cute. Others found it noisy. Their teacher, Ms. Gao, explained that the bird might be seeing its own reflection and thinking it was another bird.
The students made paper leaves and placed them on the window. The reflection became less clear. The next morning, the bird came again but did not tap as much. After a few days, it stopped coming.
The classroom became quiet again, but the students missed the bird a little. They learned that helping an animal sometimes means making it leave safely, not keeping it nearby for fun.
